title: 21 Elephants Crossed the Brooklyn Bridge to Prove It Was Safe

scenes.text: In 1884, twenty-one elephants walked across the Brooklyn Bridge.
A year earlier, a panic on the bridge had killed twelve people. Many New Yorkers were afraid it would collapse.
So showman P. T. Barnum marched his elephants across, along with seventeen camels.
The bridge held. New Yorkers cheered.
If it could hold that parade, it could hold you.
Twenty-one elephants. Zero problems. The bridge still stands today.

description:
In May 1884, P. T. Barnum led 21 elephants and 17 camels across the Brooklyn Bridge to reassure a nervous public.
A stampede on the bridge in 1883 had killed 12 people, and many feared it would collapse. The parade helped restore confidence, and the bridge is still in use today.
Would you have crossed behind the elephants? Tell us below.
first_comment: Barnum also used the walk as free advertising for his circus. Genius or shameless?
